claims.text: Under TEA's hybrid model an automated scoring engine scores written STAAR answers first, and at least 25 percent of them then go to human scorers.
claims.quote: This means that the responses are initially scored by an automated scoring engine (ASE) and at least 25 percent of student responses are then routed to human scorers.
claims.document: TEA, Scoring Process for STAAR Constructed Responses, December 2023

claims.text: Written answers on the Spanish-language STAAR are 100 percent human scored and are never scored by the engine.
claims.quote: Student responses to SCR and ECR questions for STAAR Spanish assessments are 100 percent human scored and do not get scored by the ASE.
claims.document: TEA, Scoring Process for STAAR Constructed Responses, December 2023

claims.text: When a response is sent to a human scorer, the human's score becomes the score of record.
claims.quote: Any student responses that are routed for human scoring maintain the score assigned by the human scorer as the score of record.
claims.document: TEA, Scoring Process for STAAR Constructed Responses, December 2023

claims.text: The engine is trained on student responses from field tests and on the scores humans gave those responses.
claims.quote: The ASE is trained on student responses and human scores from the field-test data.
claims.document: TEA, Scoring Process for STAAR Constructed Responses, December 2023

claims.text: TEA requires the engine to agree with human scorers at the same rate human scorers agree with one another.
claims.quote: human scorers at the same rate human scorers agree with one another and that the distribution of ASE scores is similar to the distribution of human scores.
claims.document: TEA, Scoring Process for STAAR Constructed Responses, December 2023
claims.note: The sentence starts at the foot of page 3 with the words TEA requires the ASE to agree with. A running header interrupts it, so the quote is the page 4 part.

claims.text: The engine gives a condition code to a response that is blank, uses too few words, is mostly duplicated text, is written in another language, is mostly stimulus material, uses vocabulary unlike the responses used to train the engine, or reads as off topic or off task.
claims.quote: Condition codes indicate that a response is blank, uses too few words, uses mostly duplicated text, is written in another language, consists primarily of stimulus material, uses vocabulary that does not overlap with the vocabulary in the subset of responses used to train the ASE, or uses language patterns that are reflective of off-topic or off-task responses.
claims.document: TEA, Scoring Process for STAAR Constructed Responses, December 2023

claims.text: Responses the engine marks as low confidence are often ones that fall on the border between two score points.
claims.quote: The low confidence responses are often those responses that are on the border between

claims.text: District testing personnel can ask for a student's written response to be rescored, for a fee.
